newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 24.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Irish police and RUC anti-terrorist officers played a key role in the police operation that stopped IRA plans for a bomb blitz in London.
- A curfew for teen thugs and fines for their parents are included in new legislation to be approved by the government tomorrow.
- Fee income at Ireland's largest accountancy firms rose by nearly seven percent in the past financial year to a record 212 million Irish pounds.
- The Irish government is to object to a 35 million proposal for a Hilton Hotel in Dublin city centre.
- Curfews are to be imposed on child offenders under provisions in the new Children Bill which also allows the courts to make parents pay compensation for damage caused by their children.
- MI5 and anti-terrorist police foiled what they believed were preparations for a massive pre-election bombing campaign in Britain.
- New proposals on the regulation of investment intermediaries are to be put to government by the Minister for Commerce, Science and Technology Pat Rabbitte over the next couple of months.
- Strict adherence to the Maastricht criteria for Economic and Monetary Union could drive some European economies into severe recession, Michael Smurfit, chairman of Jefferson Smurfit Group, said.
